Slide 2 is a request/response exchange, so a sequence diagram shows it and the copy says what each step saves.

arguments.source:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Cache
    participant O as Origin
    C->>O: GET /page
    O-->>C: 200 + ETag v42
    Note over C: copy goes stale
    C->>O: If-None-Match v42
    O-->>C: 304 Not Modified
    Note over C: reuse copy
arguments.caption: Revalidation with an ETag: the body travels once

arguments.slide_outline: {"title": "An ETag lets a cache confirm its copy with a 304 instead of downloading it again", "keyPoints": ["The first response carries an ETag alongside the body", "Once the copy is stale, the cache asks with If-None-Match", "Unchanged: 304 Not Modified, no body, freshness resets", "Changed: 200 with the new body and a new ETag"], "contentType": "content", "notes": "The sequence diagram shows the exchange; the copy explains what each step saves. Last-Modified / If-Modified-Since is the weaker validator."}

response.content: {"slideIndex": 1, "section": "Revalidation", "titleRegister": "label", "contents": [{"type": "text", "runs": [{"text": "An ETag turns a re-download into a 304 with no body"}]}, {"type": "text", "runs": [{"text": "The first response carries an ETag, a version tag for exactly that representation, alongside the body.", "bullet": false}, {"text": "Once the stored copy is stale, the cache sends the request again with If-None-Match and that tag.", "bullet": false}, {"text": "If nothing changed, the origin answers 304 Not Modified with no body, and the cache resets the copy's freshness.", "bullet": false}, {"text": "If it did change, the origin answers 200 with the new body and a new ETag, which the cache stores in its place.", "bullet": false}]}], "notes": "The saving is the body, not the round trip: a 304 still costs a request. Last-Modified with If-Modified-Since is the weaker, second-resolution validator."}
Slide 3 is a sequence of states a cached copy passes through, so a flow shows it.

arguments.slide_outline: {"title": "A CDN may serve stale content only when the response grants it", "keyPoints": ["stale-while-revalidate: serve stale for a window while refetching in the background (RFC 5861)", "stale-if-error: serve stale for a window when the origin fails", "must-revalidate forbids serving stale once expired", "Recap: max-age sets freshness, ETags make revalidation cheap, and stale is a choice the response makes"], "contentType": "content", "notes": "The flow shows a cached copy's life from fresh to must-refetch; the copy says which directive grants each stage."}

response.content: {"slideIndex": 2, "section": "Stale content", "titleRegister": "label", "contents": [{"type": "text", "runs": [{"text": "A CDN serves stale content only when the response allows it"}]}, {"type": "text", "runs": [{"text": "stale-while-revalidate lets the CDN answer with the stale copy for a set window while it refetches in the background.", "bullet": false}, {"text": "stale-if-error lets it keep answering with the stale copy for a set window when the origin fails or times out.", "bullet": false}, {"text": "must-revalidate forbids serving a stale copy once it has expired, whatever the CDN would otherwise prefer.", "bullet": false}, {"text": "In short: max-age sets freshness, ETags make revalidation cheap, and serving stale is a choice the response makes.", "bullet": false}]}], "notes": "Both stale directives are defined in RFC 5861; CDNs add their own overrides on top, so check the provider's documentation before relying on defaults."}
